$comment: Layer 4 - claims this repository cannot prove on its own: a physical device, the App Store, an external service. Each entry is a dated statement of what a human observed, with an expiry and a re-verify recipe, referenced from a governed document with <!-- vt-claim: attested <id> -->. An entry past its budget FAILS the gate, and so does one no document references. Device and store claims are NOT auto-detected from prose - the marker is how such a claim enters the ledger.

entries.claim: The Capacitor iOS shell is live on the App Store. Re-verify by opening the store listing and confirming the published build is at least the number in ios/.last-shipped-build
entries.attestedBy: repo owner (recorded in CLAUDE.md, Architecture / Native shell)

entries.claim: versionCode 10301 (1.3.0) sits on the Play alpha track as a DRAFT release for uk.vettrack.app, so 'blocked until the first AAB is uploaded' is no longer why the App Signing certificate is unavailable. Re-verify with the authenticated gplay CLI: `gplay edits create --package uk.vettrack.app`, then `gplay tracks list --package uk.vettrack.app --edit <id>` — expect track 'alpha' carrying release 1.3.0 with versionCodes ['10301'].
entries.evidence: Play Developer API via the authenticated gplay CLI
entries.attestedBy: agent run 2026-08-31, credentials in ~/keys (not in this repo)

entries.claim: The authenticated gplay CLI cannot read the Play App Signing certificate: no signing/cert command exists, and the sha256 returned by `gplay bundles list` is the digest of the uploaded AAB, not the certificate fingerprint. The SHA-256 for well-known-assetlinks.ts is therefore Console-only, owner-side. Re-verify with `gplay --help` and `gplay bundles --help`; this entry fails the day a certificate read is added, at which point the row becomes an agent step.
entries.evidence: gplay --help command surface; gplay bundles list output shape
